title: Continuous Heart Rate Anomaly Window
real_world_story: An ICU bedside telemetry monitor records a patient's heart rate in beats per minute once every minute over an N-minute observation shift: h_1, h_2, ..., h_N. Clinical monitoring guidelines state that acute hemodynamic instability is signaled when the spread between the maximum and minimum heart rate recorded within any contiguous time window of K minutes is greater than or equal to a critical threshold T (i.e., max(window) - min(window) >= T). The telemetry software must compute how many of the (N - K + 1) sliding time windows of length K trigger this instability alert.
problem_statement: Given an array of N integers representing consecutive heart rate readings, a window size K (1 <= K <= N), and a threshold T, count how many contiguous subsegments of length K satisfy the condition (max(subsegment) - min(subsegment) >= T).
task: Count the number of length-K windows where the difference between the maximum and minimum values is at least T.
input_format:
The first line contains three space-separated integers N, K, and T.
The second line contains N space-separated integers h_1, h_2, ..., h_N.
output_format: Print a single integer representing the number of anomalous windows.

examples.explanation:
Windows of length 3:
1. [70, 75, 95]: max=95, min=70, diff=25 >= 20 (Alert)
2. [75, 95, 80]: max=95, min=75, diff=20 >= 20 (Alert)
3. [95, 80, 60]: max=95, min=60, diff=35 >= 20 (Alert)
4. [80, 60, 65]: max=80, min=60, diff=20 >= 20 (Alert)
Total anomalous windows = 4.
In all windows of length 2, the difference between consecutive values is at most 3, which is strictly less than 15. Output 0.

real_world_takeaway: Maintaining monotonic double-ended queues allows continuous calculation of sliding window extremes in amortized O(1) time per telemetry packet.
